the most common supportive care needs of women after treatment for gynecologic cancer are sexual health and body image, and the most important predictors of supportive care needs are age, education level and the presence of sexual problems.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the sexual health of women who are survivors of gynecologic cancer.
the sexual health needs of women with a gynecologic cancer, their partners and families.
the sexual health of women with gynecologic cancer and how it can be improved.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the majority of patients with gynecologic cancer are not receiving the sexual health care they require.
sexual health needs are not met in the majority of gynecological cancer survivors, and that the current supportive care services are not adequate.
sexual problems are common in women who have had gynecologic cancer and are associated with a range of factors including age, cancer type and stage, and treatment.

sexual health care for gynecologic cancer patients is an important and often unmet need that can be addressed with a multidisciplinary team of health care providers.
